content_of_post_to_comment: made a post on here a while back about turning my socials off at 18 and struggling with the boredom, and basically every comment said the same thing, just sit in it, let yourself be bored, dont fill the gap. and honestly that advice worked. i stopped reaching for my phone every 5 seconds, started reading again, hooping, actually present now , but theres a part nobody warned me about. once the boredom settled the thing that replaced it was feeling kind of out of the loop. my friends talk about stuff someone posted or some drama and i have no clue. plans get made in group chats and stories and i find out after they already happened. at 18 everyone runs their whole social life through this stuff so being off it means youre standing slightly outside everything, and the weird part is i dont miss scrolling at all, not even a little. i just miss knowing whats going on. being in it so the boredom advice was right, i just didnt expect the next problem to be loneliness instead. for people whove been off way longer, does this part get better or do you just accept youre a little out of the loop forever. did you find another way to stay in it or did you let the looser friendships fade?
comment: I think there’s a weird adjustment period where you realize social media wasn’t just entertainment, it was the background infrastructure for everyone’s plans and conversations. I’ve seen people handle this by keeping one low-noise channel open, like a group chat or texting a few close friends, without going back to feeds. Being informed and being constantly plugged in aren’t the same thing.
